title: retire is a command
lead: `slicer retire ID --reason TEXT` retires an item exactly as `slicer remove ID --reason TEXT` does.
findings_note: outer-session wishlist 2026-10-16, item 8: reached for slicer retire, which does not exist

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: On 2026-10-16 the outer session ran `slicer retire` to retire s316 and got `invalid choice`. Retiring is `remove --reason` (`src/slicer/cli.py:3724`), whose name suggests deletion, while `retired` is the status it sets and the word the docs and render use. `remove --purge` is the deleting form.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: a `retire` subcommand sharing `cmd_remove`'s retire path, with `--reason` required, plus `--render`, `--strict`, `--force`, `--dry-run` and `--json`. It has no `--purge`. Its JSON payload and error codes are those of `remove --reason`, with `command` set to `retire`.
- `docs/commands.md`, `docs/agents.md` (the `retire` row points at `remove`'s payload), `CHANGELOG.md` under Added.
- `tests/test_remove.py` (or wherever `remove` is tested).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Retire_Reason_SameStateAsRemoveReason`: the index and history after `retire` match `remove --reason` on a twin fixture.
- `test_Retire_NoReason_Usage`
- `test_Retire_Purge_NotAccepted`

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the subcommand; docs and CHANGELOG; mutation-check (accept a missing reason).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
